instruction:
Return-Path Continuity Check

The file `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb` is a 4-layer PCB. The In1.Cu layer has a split: GND fills the left half (x = 0..40 mm) and +3V3 fills the right half (x = 40..80 mm). A high-speed signal net HS1 runs on F.Cu and crosses this split at x = 40 mm. Two stitching capacitors (CS1, CS2, each 100 nF with pads on GND and +3V3) are currently placed far from the crossing (near x = 62 mm). The file `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_dru` contains only a version header.

1. In `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb`, relocate CS1 and CS2 so each is within 3 mm of the plane-split crossing point (x = 40, y = 20).
2. In `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_dru`, add a custom DRC rule that detects return-path issues (high-speed signals crossing a plane split). The rule must have at least a `(condition...)` and a `(constraint...)` clause.
3. Also write `/home/user/Desktop/drc.report` as the native KiCad CLI DRC report generated from your final board and rules file.

Requirements:
1. CS1 and CS2 footprints must exist in `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb`.
2. Each cap must be within 3 mm Euclidean distance of the split crossing at (40, 20).
3. Both caps must retain GND and +3V3 pad assignments.
4. `/home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_dru` must parse as a valid s-expression with `(version 1)` and at least one `(rule...)` block.
5. The rule must include a `(condition...)` and a `(constraint...)` clause.

Write /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_dru, and /home/user/Desktop/drc.report.
source: Henry Ott, *Electromagnetic Compatibility Engineering* ch. 7 (return currents), KiCad 9 Official Documentation - PCB Editor / CLI (`kicad-cli pcb drc`, DRC custom rules)
